gaps.title: Dapper rejects the direct-table query-time projection arm over a column-less source
targets: all five backends (was: dotnet + persistence: dapper)
gaps.fix: RESOLVED (not as scoped). The premise below — that EF Core reads the column-less sources and Dapper merely has to catch up — was FALSE, and was the reason this sat as an adapter row. EF Core maps a `shape: document` aggregate to a hand-rolled `<Agg>Document` row type, so `o.Total` is CS1061 there too; an event-sourced source has no `DbSet` at all; a TPC base has no table. Every backend named the same missing column (node `sum(schema.orders.total)` → TS2339, JPQL `sum(e.total)`, SQLAlchemy `OrderRow.total`, Ecto `record.total`). So the refusal became UNIVERSAL: `loom.projection-columnless-source`, raised by `validateColumnlessProjectionSources` off the backend-neutral `columnlessProjectionSource` classifier (renamed from `dapperQueryProjectionGap`), and the dapper projection block + `loom.dapper-unsupported#feature` are gone. The gate is precise about the document case — a document table has a real `id` column, so `select n = count()` still emits everywhere, which is the row-count tile `scaffoldDashboard` synthesises. ORIGINAL SCOPE (still open as an emitter task, on all five backends rather than one adapter): teach the direct-table arm to read the column-less sources' actual storage — the event-log table, the jsonb blob, the concrete tables of a TPC base — and narrow the classifier as each lands.
